text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Feb 28 meeting of the National Security Council will be critical as the armed forces chief is expected to tell the president the army's unease about systematic anti-secular policies by Islamists.
- The Islamist-led government will try to defend itself in the West as Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller attends a NATO foreign ministers meeting and State Minister Abdullah Gul visits the United States.
- Conservative coalition partner Ciller says she will warn Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan over Islamist pledges which he has voiced recently.

- The ruling Islamist Welfare Party is determined to erect a mosque in Istanbul's central Taksim Square despite opposition from secularists. The city council has decided not to renew rent contracts of shops in the area.
- Turkey will ask holidaymakers their views and advice in order to shape its tourism policy.
- Tansu Ciller's hopes rest with her coalition partner as parliament prepares to vote on two reports regarding alleged corruption involving her.
- Turkey's forestry product industry is failing to compete with those in the European Union.
- The Directorate of Religious Affairs asks the state for a television channel to educate uninformed Moslems about Islam.
